text:
oncall-bot: 🚨 ALERT: GPU queue growth detected for pool gpu-prod-a. queue_length > 10k sustained for 3m, token_throttle firing. creating incident INC-2026-042 at 2094001111

oncall-bot: autoscaler reported repeated scale attempts but no new GPUs attached for last 6m (retries=8). potential autoscale deadlock. tagging #oncall and #eng-runtime

ana (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing SRE. paging @lee and @sam. setting priority to P1.

sam (infra): looking at autoscaler logs now. seeing repeated API 409: "pool_scale_limit_exceeded" followed by "Scale request queued" then no node allocation. snippet:```json
{"time":"2094001150","msg":"scale_request","pool":"gpu-prod-a","requested":4,"limit":8,"current":8}```

jay (serving): Concurrently, serving runtime metrics show batch processing latency spike and a sudden drop in throughput (tokens/sec). 95th lat went from 110ms -> 1.4s in the last 4m. prefix_cache hitrate jumped to 22% -> 5% since 2094000900. suspecting caching regression.

marta (ml): I pushed a change earlier to continuous-batching parameters in PR #4721 around 2093999000 — changed batching_window_ms from 8 -> 200 to improve throughput for long tails. that could be creating huge batches and evicting KV cache entries more often.

lee (sre): that explains eviction. large batches extend seq lengths and blow the KV cache working set. infra: can we temporarily override autoscaler caps and add capacity? we need breathing room to finish rollback.

sam (infra): I can force-add nodes but we still risk the runtime being unable to keep up because of batch-induced cache misses. proposing two-step mitigation: 1) revert batching_window flag to 8ms, 2) temporarily bump pool max to 12 to drain queue.

ana (oncall): Agreed. Prioritize rollback first (fast), then manual scale if queue not falling. ACTIONS: @sam revert PR, @lee manual scale, @jay validate serving metrics, @marta confirm config.

sam (infra): starting revert now.```bash
# rollback PR revert
git revert --no-commit 7b3c9f2 && deploy rollout continuous-batching-service --env=prod
```ETA ~2m for deploy trigger.

infra-bot: scale request received: pool=gpu-prod-a, delta=+4, requested_by=sam, reason="incident INC-2026-042 - manual override". estimated attach time 75s.

lee (sre): issuing manual scale:```bash
redwood infra scale-pool --pool gpu-prod-a --count 12 --reason "INC-2026-042 manual scale to drain"
```Doing now.

jay (serving): interesting logs from runtime:```
[2094001185] batch_size=512 latency=1800ms kv_cache_evictions=4123 prefix_cache_miss_rate=0.78
[2094001200] batch_size=1024 latency=2300ms kv_cache_evictions=8921 prefix_cache_miss_rate=0.82
```Prefix cache TTL shows 0 in config (was supposed to be 3600s). Looks like a bad default in the new batching config.

marta (ml): ack — my change accidentally removed the prefix_cache_ttl override in the feature flag. that's on me. rolling that flag to restore TTL=3600s.

sam (infra): scale completed: 4 nodes attached, pool size now 12. queue length dropped 20% in 60s but still above acceptable. continuing.

ana (oncall): Customer impact assessment: premium customers seeing elevated latency and ~14% request throttling (token throttle). non-premium experiencing higher error rate (~2%). drafting customer-facing note for CS now.

infra-bot: Incident update: INC-2026-042 | state=mitigating | severity=P1 | impacted_clusters=gpu-prod-a | included_teams=serving,infra,ml,sre

lee (sre): routing change applied to divert enterprise traffic:```json
{"route":"customer_tier==enterprise","target_pool":"dedicated-enterprise"}```Traffic for tagged enterprise customers now flows to dedicated pool. observing 95th latency for enterprise drop to 300ms.

jay (serving): after revert + TTL restore, prefix_cache_miss_rate back down to 6% and token throughput rising. batch sizes are back to ~32-64. serving latency returning to baseline.

marta (ml): opened followup PR to add a guard in CI: continuous-batching changes must include explicit prefix_cache_ttl and a canary rollout. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/4750

sam (infra): opened autoscaler hardcap safety ticket: allow manual scale bypass for emergencies and add alert when scale_request_retries > 5. https://tickets/redwood/INC-2026-042-ops

ana (oncall): Good work team. Current status: mitigated — queue draining, traffic rerouted, revert rolled out. still monitoring for 1h. owners: postmortem @marta, followups @sam and @lee. Handoff to @lee for overnight watch. Please update the incident doc with timeline and actions.

infra-bot: INC-2026-042 created successor: postmortem assigned to marta. next update scheduled at 2094003300.

sam (infra): quick note: we should add a canary metric for prefix_cache_hitrate to the autoscaler decision logic — autoscaler should not scale down when cache miss rate > 0.2. filing that as a followup.

lee (sre): handing off monitoring to next oncall. I will keep an eye on the dashboard and escalate if queue growth returns.

ana (oncall): thanks everyone. final summary for now: root cause = continuous-batching parameter regression that indirectly caused prefix cache evictions + prefix_cache_ttl removal -> throughput collapse; secondary cause = autoscaler hit pool cap and failed to provide breathing room quickly. mitigations = revert batching change, restore TTL, manual pool scale, route enterprise traffic, create followups.

oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-042 | status=acknowledged -> mitigated | first_seen=2094001111 | mitigated_at=2094002280 | severity=P1

sam (infra): I'll open the long-form incident doc and include command history, metrics, and the draft customer note. passing to postmortem owner @marta.

marta (ml): will own postmortem, will schedule blameless review and add e2e to prevent missing TTL or batching CLIs. thanks team. :heart:
